h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to classify settings as strong, weak, neutral or harmful, and to identify which settings can disconnect other parts from the outcome. Propose hypotheses only of two kinds. Self-conditioning: the edit's effect depends on the value it replaces, being more negative when that value is strong and more positive when it is empty or harmful. Disconnection: when the edited part cannot influence the outcome, its effect shrinks toward zero, so the direction is lower if the edit usually helps and higher if it usually hurts. Directions refer to the signed effect. For each hypothesis, state the edit's usual sign and a one-sentence mechanism. Cover varied edit fields and values. The critic should replace any hypothesis with an uncertain usual sign, competing effects or reliance on partial redundancy.

hyps.why: Edge 1 feeds node 2, whose only exit is edge 5, so with edge 5 = none the usually positive conv edit cannot reach the output and its effect shrinks toward zero.
Edge 2 also ends at node 2, so edge 5 = none disconnects it and removes the usual conv gain.
Edge 0 = none leaves node 1 with no input, so the usually helpful conv on edge 4 processes nothing and its effect vanishes.
Node 1 is dead when edge 0 = none, so a conv on edge 2 (which usually helps) has no signal to act on.
Removing edge 1 usually hurts, but when edge 5 is none edge 1 is already disconnected, so the removal costs nothing and the signed effect moves up toward zero.
Setting the direct input-to-output edge to conv_3x3 gains most when it replaces an empty edge because it adds a new path rather than upgrading an existing one.
Edge 5 = none cuts node 2 from the output, so conv_3x3 restores connectivity for edges 1 and 2 and gains far more than it would replacing a working op.
Edge 0 = none disconnects node 1 and edges 2 and 4 from the input, so conv_3x3 here reconnects them and gains much more than a kernel upgrade would.
With edge 0 = none node 1 receives no input so edge 4 is already dead, and removing it costs nothing whereas removing a live edge normally hurts.
With edge 0 = none node 1 is empty so edge 2 carries nothing, and removing it has no cost compared with the usual loss from deleting a live edge.
